title: C-flat Major Piano Chord (Cb): Notes, Inversions & PDF
description: Read C-flat major as C-flat, E-flat and G-flat. Match C-flat4 to the B3 key, compare inversions and print an enharmonic reference.
user_task: Locate this exact triad and compare its three bass positions.
questions: Is C-flat major different from C major?
Does the keyboard builder recognize enharmonic choices?

blocks.heading: Notes and keyboard position
blocks.body: C-flat major contains C-flat, E-flat and G-flat. On an equal-tempered piano, its pitch classes match B, D-sharp and F-sharp. The displayed root-position example is C♭4–E♭4–G♭4. Numbers after note letters identify octaves, not fingers. Use the diagram, note list and bass label together; Play chord sounds the selected notes together, while the note-by-note control sounds them from low to high.
blocks.evidence_status: [已核实] rules; [推断] register and original teaching example

blocks.heading: What to notice
blocks.body: A flat sign does not guarantee a black key. C-flat uses the white B key immediately below the written C. In this root example, C♭4 is the same sounding key as B3, not B4. C-flat to E-flat is a major third and C-flat to G-flat a perfect fifth. The three flat signs preserve the root–third–fifth letter pattern C–E–G. Replacing only one label with its sharp equivalent would obscure that spelling.
blocks.evidence_status: [推断] original explanation from preserved note data and cited rules

blocks.heading: Compare three positions
blocks.body: Read each bass note before selecting a position. The root-position example starts with C♭; first inversion starts with E♭; second inversion starts with G♭. The chord tones stay the same. These are independently chosen reference registers, not an ascending exercise. Switching a position must update the selected note order, diagram, sound and current-print snapshot together. Hand numbers, when available, apply only to the root example.
